name: Lateral Bound
summary: A plyometric drill where you explosively push off one foot sideways and stick the landing on the opposite leg to develop lateral power and deceleration control.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart on a clear, non-slip surface.
Shift your weight onto one leg and slightly flex the ankle, knee, and hip into an athletic ready stance.
Lift the non-weight-bearing foot slightly off the floor, keeping your torso upright and core engaged.
steps: Hinge slightly at the hip and load your support leg like a compressed spring.
Explosively push off the floor laterally, driving sideways across your body using your hip and lower leg.
Land softly on the opposite foot, absorbing the impact by bending through the ankle, knee, and hip in a controlled quarter-squat.
Pause for one to two seconds to establish complete balance and stability before repeating the bound back in the opposite direction.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you load the stance leg, exhale forcefully during the lateral drive, and breathe steadily while stabilizing the landing.

common_faults.fault: Landing with a stiff knee and hip, creating excessive joint impact.
common_faults.correction: Actively absorb force upon landing by flexing through the hip, knee, and ankle into a soft athletic position.

common_faults.fault: Knee valgus where the landing knee collapses inward.
common_faults.correction: Engage the glutes and keep the landing knee stacked directly over the second toe.

common_faults.fault: Rushing immediately into the next jump without stabilizing.
common_faults.correction: Hold the landing for a distinct one- to two-second pause to develop deceleration mechanics before bounding again.

precautions: Ensure ample floor space free of equipment and slippery surfaces.
Progress jump distance gradually to ensure landing control before prioritizing power.
